title: Randomized throttle fuzz run — notes (Mikaela)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick fuzzing of throttle/priority heuristics under randomized client arrival and token-length variance. Want to see where p99 jumps when two lanes contend and KV cache hit fluctuates.

Hypothesis:
- Small jitter (10-50ms) in request arrival combined with random short/long token ratios will cause transient p99 spikes due to batching misalignment and KV cache churn. Expected: p50 stable, p95 small bump, p99 large tail.

Setup:
- Binary: rbk-loadgen v0.8 (custom) running from 3 agents (eu-west1/cpu-32).
- Target overall QPS: 120, 360, 720 (three phases).
- Payload distribution: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 30% long (>=1024 tokens).
- Inter-arrival model: randomized Poisson with added jitter uniform[0,50ms].
- Priority lanes: foreground (token-limit 256) and background. Throttle policy: fractional token-buckets + preemptive steal.
- KV cache: warm/unwarm toggles: ran 50% runs with cache-primed and 50% with 10% miss flood.
- Metrics collected: per-request latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), GPU util, kernel-queue-depth, batch sizes, kv-hit-rate.

Command snippets:
- start load: ./rbk-loadgen --qps 360 --agents 3 --dist short:0.7,long:0.3 --jitter 50 --seed 202602
- prometheus tag: fuzz/run-2026-02-20-mikaela

Results (summary table, representative run, qps=360, cache warm):
- Overall QPS: 360
- p50: 18ms
- p90: 42ms
- p95: 86ms
- p99: 410ms
- error%: 0.6% (timeouts and canceled preemptions)
- avg batch size: 6.2 tokens per request equivalent, but longs increased kernel batching lag
- kv-hit-rate: 89% (cache primed)
- GPU util: 64% (spiky), kernel-queue-depth median 3, 95th 12

Results (cache miss flood):
- p50: 22ms
- p95: 180ms
- p99: 1.2s
- error%: 2.8% (timeouts increased)
- avg batch size similar, but more micro-batches triggered by cache misses

Observations / informal notes:
- p99 events correlate tightly with a burst of long requests that arrive within ~20–60ms of each other and find an empty kv-cache for prefixes (miss cascade).
- When background lane preemption engages, we see head-of-line blocking for a few foreground requests while kernel scheduling swaps - these create long tails.
- Small random jitter actually amplified misalignment for batching windows at 4–8ms thresholds. Turning jitter down to 5ms reduces p99 by ~30% on some runs.
- Increasing the max batch timeout from 8ms -> 12ms reduced p99 but increased median by ~5–7ms (tradeoff ok for some SLAs).
- Observed a repeatable pattern: sequence of long, short, long causes the kernel to spin up extra sub-batches that add ~200–400ms per long in the worst case.

Quick conclusions:
1) KV cache priming matters—cache-miss floods are the single largest multiplier for tail latency in our synthetic mixes.
2) Batching window tuning and jitter control together can mitigate a chunk of p99 but with cost to p50. Consider adaptive window: increase when queue-age low, shrink on detected long-request waves.
3) Preemptive steal policy of background lane needs guardrails: limit the number of simultaneous steals per GPU and prefer stealing from same-shard to avoid kernel thrash.

Next steps / experiments to run:
- Repeat runs with adaptive-batch-window (prototype branch) and measure p99 delta at qps 720.
- Run longer-duration (60m) tests to see whether rare alignment events happen less/more often over time.
- Add synthetic cache-warming agent that polls popular prefixes to see if we can reduce miss cascades without large extra cost.
- Try deterministic arrival micro-bursts (e.g., 4 requests at 10ms intervals) to reproduce worst-case tail reliably.

Notes to self:
- Upload full traces -> s3://redwood-inference-temp/fuzz-runs/2026-02-20/mikaela/ (raw histograms + flamegraphs).
- Link to quick Grafana dash: /d/latency-fuzz/fuzz-2026-02-20 (local copy).
- Share with Samir and SRE on Monday for follow-up.

Unresolved questions:
- Is the miss-cascade mostly due to prefix eviction policy or client diversity causing new prefixes? Need per-prefix access histograms.
- How do kernels behave when mixed quantized vs full-precision models in same pool? Might be additional context-switch cost.

End of note.
